However, John got his bearings again and the Harney party found the camp of Chakaika and the '[Spanish Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Indians "Spanish Indians")'. Dressed as Indians, the soldiers approached the camp early in the morning, achieving surprise. Chakaika was outside the camp when the attack started. He started to run and then stopped and turned to face the soldiers, offering his hand, but one of the soldiers shot and killed him. There was a brief fight during which some of the Indians escaped. Harney had two of the captured warriors hanged, and had Chakaika's body hung beside them. Harney and his men returned to Fort Dallas after twelve days in the [Everglades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everglades "Everglades"). Harney had lost one soldier killed. His command had killed four Indians in action and hanged five more. The Legislative Council of Florida presented Harney with a commendation and a sword, and Harney was soon given command of the [Second Dragoons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2nd_Cavalry_Regiment_(United_States) "2nd Cavalry Regiment (United States)").[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-97)

Armistead had US$55,000 ($1.8 million in 2025 dollars) to use for bribing chiefs to surrender. In November 1840, General Armistead met at Fort King with [Thlocklo Tustenuggee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thlocklo_Tustenuggee "Thlocklo Tustenuggee"), a Muscogee speaker known as "Tiger Tail", and [Halleck Tustenuggee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Halleck_Tustenuggee "Halleck Tustenuggee"), a Mikasuki speaker. Armistead was authorized by Washington to offer each leader $5,000 ($115,023) to bring their followers in for transportation west, and to concede land in the south of Florida to those remaining. However, Colonel [Ethan A. Hitchcock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethan_A._Hitchcock_(general) "Ethan A. Hitchcock (general)") recorded in his diary, with considerable frustration, that the General instead pocketed these proposals and insisted the chiefs agree to the terms of the Payne's Landing treaty. Moreover, while talking peace, he secretly sent a force threatening Halleck's people at his home. After several days as guests of the Army both chiefs fled in the middle of the night on November 14, 1840.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-98) Echo Emathla, a Tallahassee chief, surrendered, but most of the Tallahassee, under Thlocklo Tustenuggee, did not. The Mikasukis, led by Coosa Tustenuggee and Halleck Tustenuggee, continued to operate in the northern part of the Florida peninsula. Coosa Tustenuggee finally accepted $5,000 for bringing in his sixty people. Lesser chiefs received $200 ($4,601), and every warrior $30 ($690) and a rifle. Coacoochee took advantage of Armistead's willingness to negotiate. In March 1841, he agreed to bring in his followers in two or three months. During that time, he appeared at several forts, presenting the pass given to him by Armistead, and demanding food and liquor. On one visit to Fort Pierce, Coacoochee demanded a horse to ride to Fort Brooke. The fort commander gave him one, along with five and one-half gallons of whiskey.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-99)

By the spring of 1841, Armistead had sent 450 Seminoles west. Another 236 were at Fort Brooke awaiting transportation. Armistead estimated that 120 warriors had been shipped west during his tenure, and that there were no more than 300 warriors left in Florida. In May 1841, Halleck Tustenuggee sent word that he would be bringing his band in to surrender.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-100)

## Colonel Worth takes charge

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Second_Seminole_War&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Colonel Worth takes charge")]

In May 1841, Armistead was replaced by Col. [William Jenkins Worth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Jenkins_Worth "William Jenkins Worth") as commander of Army forces in Florida. Due to the unpopularity of the war in the nation and in Congress, Worth had to cut back. The war was costing US$93,300 per month in addition to the pay of the regular soldiers. [John T. Sprague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_T._Sprague "John T. Sprague"), Worth's aide, believed that some civilians were trying to deliberately prolong the war in order to stay on the government payroll. Nearly 1,000 civilian employees of the Army were released, and smaller commands were consolidated. Worth then ordered his men out on what would now be called '[search and destroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Search_and_destroy "Search and destroy")' missions during the summer. These efforts effectively drove the Seminoles out of their old stronghold in the Cove of the Withlacoochee. Much of the rest of northern Florida was also cleared by these methods.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-101)

On May 1, 1841, Lieutenant [William Tecumseh Sherman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Tecumseh_Sherman "William Tecumseh Sherman") was assigned to escort Coacoochee to a meeting at Fort Pierce. (The fort was named for Colonel [Benjamin Kendrick Pierce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benjamin_Kendrick_Pierce "Benjamin Kendrick Pierce"), who oversaw its construction.) After washing and dressing in his best (which included a vest with a bullet hole and blood on it), Coacoochee asked Sherman to give him silver in exchange for a one-dollar bill from the Bank of Tallahassee. At the meeting Major [Thomas Childs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Childs "Thomas Childs") agreed to give Coacoochee thirty days to bring in his people for transportation west. Coacoochee's people came and went freely at the fort for the rest of the month, while Childs became convinced that Coachoochee would renege on his agreement. Childs asked for and received permission to seize Coacoochee. On June 4 he arrested Coachoochee and fifteen of his followers. Lieutenant Colonel William Gates ordered that Coacoochee and his men be shipped immediately to New Orleans. When Colonel Worth learned of this, he ordered the ship to return to Tampa Bay, as he intended to use Coacoochee to persuade the rest of the Seminoles to surrender.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-102)

Colonel Worth offered bribes worth about US$8,000 to Coacoochee. As Coacoochee had no real hope of escaping, he agreed to send out messengers urging the Seminoles to move west. The chiefs still active in the northern part of the Florida peninsula, Halleck Tustenuggee, Tiger Tail, Nethlockemathla, and Octiarche, met in council and agreed to kill any messengers from the whites. The southern chiefs seemed to have learned of this decision, and supported it. However, when one messenger appeared at a council of Holata Mico, Sam Jones, Otulkethlocko, Hospetarke, Fuse Hadjo and Passacka, he was made prisoner, but not killed.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-103)

A total of 211 Seminoles surrendered as a result of Coacoochee's messages, including most of his own band. Hospetarke was drawn into a meeting at Camp Ogden (near the mouth of the Peace River) in August and he and 127 of his band were captured. As the number of Seminoles in Florida decreased, it became easier for those left to stay hidden. In November the Third Artillery moved into the [Big Cypress Swamp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Cypress_National_Preserve "Big Cypress National Preserve") and burned a few villages. Some of the Seminoles in southern Florida gave up after that, and turned themselves in for transportation west.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-104)

Seminoles were still scattered throughout most of Florida. One band that had been reduced to starvation surrendered in northern Florida near the Apalachicola River in 1842. Further east, however, bands led by Halpatter Tustenuggee, Halleck Tustenuggee and Chitto Hadjo raided [Mandarin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandarin,_Florida "Mandarin, Florida") and other settlements along the lower (i.e., northern) St. Johns River. On April 19, 1842, a column of 200 soldiers led by First Lieutenant [George A. McCall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_A._McCall "George A. McCall") found a group of Seminole warriors in the Pelchikaha Swamp, about thirty miles south of Fort King. There was a brief fire-fight and then the Seminoles disappeared into a hammock. Halleck Tustenuggee was held prisoner when he showed up at Fort King for a talk. Part of his band was caught when they visited the fort, and Lieutenant McCall captured the rest of Halleck's band in their camp.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-105)

## The war winds down

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Second_Seminole_War&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: The war winds down")]

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/33/1842seminolereservation.png/250px-1842seminolereservation.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1842seminolereservation.png)

The remaining Seminoles in Florida were allowed to stay on an informal reservation in southwest Florida at the end of the Second Seminole War in 1842.

Colonel Worth recommended early in 1842 that the remaining Seminoles be left in peace if they would stay in southern Florida. Worth eventually received authorization to leave the remaining Seminoles on an informal reservation in southwestern Florida, and to declare an end to the war on a date of his choosing. At this time there were still several diverse bands of Indians in Florida. [Billy Bowlegs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Bowlegs "Billy Bowlegs") was the head of a large band of Seminoles living near Charlotte Harbor. Sam Jones led a band of Mikasukis that lived in the Everglades near Fort Lauderdale. North of Lake Okeechobee was a band of Muskogees led by Chipco. Another Muskogee band, led by Tiger Tail, lived near Tallahassee. Finally, in northern Florida there was a band of Creeks led by Octiarche which had fled from Georgia in 1836.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-106)

In August 1842, Congress passed the [Armed Occupation Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armed_Occupation_Act "Armed Occupation Act"), which provided free land to settlers who improved the land and were prepared to defend themselves from Indians. In many ways this act prefigured the [Homestead Act of 1862](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homestead_Act_of_1862 "Homestead Act of 1862"). Heads of households could claim 160 acres (0.6 km 2) of land south of a line running across the northern part of the peninsula. They had to 'prove' their claim by living on the land for five years and clearing 5 acres (20,000 m 2). However, they could not claim land within two miles (3.2 km) of a military post. A total of 1,317 grants totaling 210,720 acres (853 km 2) were registered in 1842 and 1843.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-107)

In the last action of the war, General William Bailey and prominent planter Jack Bellamy led a posse of 52 men on a three-day pursuit of a small band of Tiger Tail's braves who had been attacking pioneers, surprising their swampy encampment and killing all 24. William Wesley Hankins, at sixteen the youngest of the posse, accounted for the last of the kills and was acknowledged as having fired the last shot of the Second Seminole War.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-108)

Also in August 1842, Worth met with the chiefs still in Florida. Each warrior was offered a rifle, money and one year's worth of rations if they moved west. Some accepted the offer, but most hoped to eventually move to the reservation in southwest Florida. Believing that the remaining Indians in Florida would either go west or move to the reservation, Worth declared the war to be at an end on August 14, 1842. Worth then went on ninety-days leave, leaving command to Colonel Josiah Vose. The Army in Florida consisted at this point of parts of three regiments, totaling 1,890 men. Attacks on white settlers continued even as far north as the area around Tallahassee. Otiarche and Tiger Tail had not indicated what they would do. Complaints from Florida caused the War Department to order Vose to take action against the bands still off the reservation, but Vose argued that breaking the pledges made to the Indians would have bad results, and the War Department accepted his arguments. In early October a major hurricane struck [Cedar Key](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedar_Key,_Florida "Cedar Key, Florida"), where the Army headquarters had been located, and the Indians would no longer visit it.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-109)

Worth returned to Florida at the beginning of November 1842. He soon decided that Tiger Tail and Otiarche had taken too long to make up their minds on what to do, and ordered that they be brought in. Tiger Tail was so ill that he had to be carried on a litter, and he died in New Orleans waiting for transportation to the Indian territory. The other Indians in northern Florida were also captured and sent west. By April 1843, only one regiment, the Eighth Infantry, was still in Florida. In November 1843 Worth reported that the only Indians left in Florida were 42 Seminole warriors, 33 Mikasukis, 10 Creeks and 10 Tallahassees, with women and children bringing the total to about 300. Worth also stated that these Indians were all living on the reservation and were no longer a threat to the white population of Florida.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-110)

## Costs

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Second_Seminole_War&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Costs")]

Mahon cites estimates of US$30,000,000 to $40,000,000 as the cost of the Second Seminole War, but knew of no analysis of the actual cost. Congress appropriated funds for the 'suppression of Indian hostilities', but the costs of the [Creek War of 1836](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creek_War_of_1836 "Creek War of 1836") are included in that. An inquiry in extravagance in naval operations found that the Navy had spent about US$511,000 on the war. The investigation did find questionable expenditures. Among other things, while the Army had bought dugout canoes for $10 to $15 apiece, the Navy spent an average of $226 per canoe. The number of Army, Navy and Marine regulars who served in Florida is given as 10,169. About 30,000 militiamen and volunteers also served in the war.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-autogenerated1-6)

By the spring 1841, the paymaster general issued a report that found the U.S. government had issued $2,500,000 in payroll to regular army soldiers and an additional $3,500,000 in payroll to citizen soldiers.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-111)

Sources agree that the U.S. Army officially recorded 1,466 deaths in the Second Seminole War, mostly from disease. The number killed in action is less clear. Mahon reports 328 regular Army killed in action, while Missall reports that Seminoles killed 269 officers and men. Almost half of those deaths occurred in the [Dade Massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dade_Massacre "Dade Massacre"), [Battle of Lake Okeechobee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Lake_Okeechobee "Battle of Lake Okeechobee") and Harney Massacre. Similarly, Mahon reports 69 deaths for the Navy while Missall reports 41 for the U.S. Navy and Marine Corps, but adds others may have died after being sent out of Florida as _incurable_. Mahon and the Florida Board of State Institutions agree that 55 volunteer officers and men were killed by the Seminoles, while Missall says the number is unknown. There is no figure for how many militiamen and volunteers died of disease or accident, however.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-ReferenceA-112)

The number of white civilians, Seminoles and Black Seminoles killed is uncertain. A northern newspaper carried a report that more than 80 civilians were killed by Indians in Florida in 1839. Nobody was keeping a cumulative account of the number of Indians and Black Seminoles killed, or the number who died of starvation or other privations caused by the war. The people shipped west did not fare well, either. By the end of 1843, 3,824 Indians (including 800 Black Seminoles) had been shipped from Florida to what became the [Indian Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Territory "Indian Territory"). They were initially settled on the Creek Reservation, which created tensions. The next year, the Florida people numbered 3,136. As of 1962, their numbers had dropped to 2,343 Seminoles in the Indian Territory and perhaps some 1,500 in Florida.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-ReferenceA-112)

## Aftermath

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Second_Seminole_War&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Aftermath")]

Peace had come to Florida for a while. The Natives were mostly staying on the reservation, but there were minor clashes. The Florida authorities continued to press for removal of all Natives from Florida. The Natives tried to limit their contacts with the [American settlers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_pioneer "American pioneer") as much as possible.

As time went on there were more serious incidents. The government resolved once more to remove all Indians from Florida, and applied increasing pressure on the Seminoles until they struck back, starting the Third Seminole War of 1855–1858.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-113)

### [Martin van Buren](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/people/president/martin-van-buren)

8th President of the United States:1837 ‐ 1841

# Martin Van Buren Event Timeline

March 04, 1837

**Martin Van Buren (8) Event Timeline**
**03/04/1837 – 03/04/1841**
05/22/1835 Democratic National Convention in Baltimore Selects Vice President Martin Van Buren as Presidential Nominee.
05/29/1835 Van Buren [formally accepts the nomination](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/message-accepting-the-democratic-presidential-nomination).
11/08/1836[Election Day](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/statistics/elections/1836). Martin Van Buren wins 57.8% of the Electoral College and 50.8% of the popular vote.
12/07/1836 Electors cast their ballots.
**1837**
02/08/1837 Electoral votes tabulated by Congress.
03/04/1837[Inaugural Address](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/inaugural-address-28). Much of Van Buren’s address is spent paying tribute to the Presidents before him.
03/27/1837 US Secretary of State John Forsyth advises that treaties with Mexico preclude US annexation of Texas.
03/28/1837[Proclamation 43C—Extinguishing Title for Indian Lands Between the State of Missouri and the Missouri River](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/proclamation-43-c-extinguishing-title-for-indian-lands-between-the-state-missouri-and-the). The federal government extinguishes all Native American land titles between Missouri and the Missouri River. Native American communities are removed after the United States claimed ownership of the land.
05/10/1837 The Panic of 1837, a financial crisis caused by reckless credit policies for Western land, drives the United States into a recession. The lack of a centralized national bank leaves many local banks to fail.
05/15/1837[Proclamation 43D](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/proclamation-43-d-convening-extra-session-the-congress)--Convening an Extra Session of the Congress in a session to begin 09/04/1837 (see below).
06/27/1837 Receives a set of [Resolves](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/state-maine-resolves-relative-the-northeastern-boundary) from officials in the State of Maine seeking assistance and support in resisting British "usurpations and encroachments," and urging the governor to call on the President to survey and explore the northeastern boundary of the state according to the treaty of 1783.
08/04/1837 The Minister of the Texas Republic [proposes annexation](https://www.tshaonline.org/handbook/entries/annexation) of Texas to the United States.
08/05/1837 Rejects the Republic of Texas’ proposal to annex Texas. Van Buren fears that annexing Texas would compel Mexico to retaliate; cause controversy by adding to slave territory.
09/04/1837 In [Special Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-session-message-7) opening a special session of Congress, calls for Congress to deal with the financial crisis. Suggested actions include a suspension of specie payments.
09/30/1937 By [Special Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-4035), provides the House of Representative with papers relating to the proposed Annexation of Texas. ([View pdf document i](https://www.google.com/books/edition/Documents_Relating_to_the_Foreign_Relati/b64TAAAAYAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22to+whom+was+referred+a+resolution+of+the+House+of+Representatives,+dated+the+13th+instant,+requesting%22&pg=RA4-PA94-IA3&printsec=frontcover)ncluding the papers referenced in this Special Message.)
11/12/1837 Newspapers report expectation of immigration to Vermont from Canada due to "serious apprehensions of disturbances in Canada (_Daily Pittsburgh Gazette, 11/13/1837, p. 2)_
11/18/1837 Further newspaper reports of armed conflict in Canada by groups opposed to British rule. (_Daily Pittsburgh Gazette, 11/27/1837, p. 2_
12/05/1837[First Annual Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/first-annual-message-4). Expresses concern about relations with Britain concerning the Maine borderlands. Discusses unsettled US claims against Mexico but makes no mention of the Republic of Texas. Advocates for an independent Treasury system.
12/05/1837 Canadian politician and firebrand [William Lyon Mackenzie](https://www.thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/mackenzie-william-lyon) attempts, near Toronto, to launch a popular rebellion against British colonial rule. Many in the US sympathized with the rebellion and hoped that eventually Canada would become part of the United States. Mackenzie later established a rebel force on Navy Island, not far from Niagara Falls.
12/21/1837[Announces construction of an independent Treasury in order to hold federal funds](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-4044).
12/29/1837 The _Caroline,_ an American steamship that was providing supplies to Canadian rebels on Navy Island (12/05/1837), [is seized by the British-backed Canadian militia](https://www.lawfareblog.com/caroline-affair), set afire, and set adrift to float over the Niagara Falls. At least one American was killed during the raid. News of this event reaches Van Buren on 01/04/1838. In subsequent years, the incident will become important in international law as an instance of "anticipatory self-defense" on the part of the British.
**1838**
01/05/1838 In a [Special Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-4045) to the Congress, expresses concern that existing laws are insufficient to guarantee protection of American borders.
01/05/1838[Proclamation 45A—Neutrality With Respect to Canadian Affairs](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/proclamation-45-neutrality-with-respect-canadian-affairs). Emphasizes a peaceful response to the conflict arising from the _Caroline_ incident.
03/12/1838 In [_Kendall v. United States_](https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/37/524/)the Supreme Court decides 9-0 decides against an expansive view of Presidential power. "To contend that the obligations imposed on the President to see the laws faithfully executed, implies a power to forbid their execution; is a novel construction of the constitution, and is entirely inadmissible."
04/25/1838[Co nvention between the United States and the Republic of Texas](https://avalon.law.yale.edu/19th_century/tex38-2.asp) establishes a commission to survey and mark the international boundary.
05/02/1838 In a [Special Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-3229) to the House, addresses d ispute over attacks on civilian steamboats between Mexico and America.
05/10/1838 In a [Special Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-3298) to the House, suggests that financial difficulties threaten to make the government insolvent.
05/21/1838 In a [Special Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-3408) to the Congress, addresses issues of communication to the Cherokee nation, asking them to move peacefully to the West.
06/12/1838 Signs Act dividing Territory of Wisconsin to establish Territorial Government of Iowa ([5 Stat 235](http://uscode.house.gov/statviewer.htm?volume=5&page=235)).
08/18/1838[The United States Exploring Expedition,](https://www.si.edu/object/united-states-exploring-expedition-1838-1842:auth_exp_fbr_EACE0051) also known as the Wilkes Expedition, departs Norfolk, Virginia. It was commissioned to survey and explore the Pacific Ocean and South Seas. The five ships and crews were provided by the U.S. Navy. The expedition returned in June 1842 having collected vast quantities of flora and fauna that eventually formed the core of the Smithsonian Institution collection (1858).
11/21/1838[Proclamation—Neutrality With Respect to Canadian Affairs](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/proclamation-neutrality-with-respect-canadian-affairs). Van Buren furthers neutrality with Canada, issuing another Proclamation stating that the American government will not assist any Americans engaged in criminal activities with Canada.
12/03/1838 In a Special Message to Congress,delivers his [Second Annual State of the Union Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/second-annual-message-4).
**1839**
02/27/1839[Special Message to Congress regarding conflict with British in the state of Maine](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-3312). The "Aroostook conflict" occurred after a government formed a militia in Maine that forcefully removed trespassers from above the border in New Brunswick. Van Buren explains that a peaceful resolution must be drawn between the nations or seasonal conflict is inevitable.
03/03/1839 Signs Act giving the President additional Powers for the defense of the United States against invasion ([5 Stat 355](https://uscode.house.gov/statviewer.htm?volume=5&page=355)). Specifically refers to any attempt by Great Britain to enforce its claim on parts of the state of Maine. Authorizes the President to call for up to 50,000 volunteers in the event of conflict.
03/05/1839[Vetoes joint resolution as it was not properly certified by the clerk of the House in which it originated.](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/veto-message-478)Explicitly does not address the substance. This is the only veto of Van Buren’s Presidency.
03/21/1839 The so-called Aroostook War concerning the boundary between Maine and Canada end in a truce negotiated by General Winfield Scott under instructions from the President. The final disposition of the border is not settled until 1842 and the Webster-Ashburton Treaty.
04/11/1839 A Convention for the Adjustment of Claims between US citizens and the Government of Mexico is signed in Washington. Creates a commission to adjudicate claims. This convention is ratified by the President 04/07/1840 and proclaimed 04/08/1840. ([Link to pdf text of the Convention](https://www.google.com/books/edition/Mexican_Claims/549chErQ0aYC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=whereas+the+parties+to+said+convention+are+still,+and+equally,+desirous+of+terminating+the+discussion&pg=PA44&printsec=frontcover))
05/13/1839 In a [Special Message to the Senate](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-4092), reports compensation by Great Britain for the brigs, _Enterprise_, _Encomium_, and _Comet_ in which slaves were captured by the British territory of the Bermuda and Bahamas islands.
08/24/1839 U.S.S. Washington seizes a ship, [the _Amistad_](https://amistadcenter.org/the-amistad-rebellion/), carrying slaves, off of Long Island. These events become a highly visible controversy about slavery.
11/13/1839 A Convention of Abolitionists was held in Warsaw, NY and nominated James G. Birney for President. He declined the nomination but received over 7600 votes in the 1840 election.
12/02/1839[Third Annual State of the Union Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/third-annual-message-4). Congratulates the Treasury on its successful handling of the Panic of 1837 and urges against the evils of the federal government accruing debt. Van Buren also urges Congress to pass a law to make public officials using public funds for private purposes a crime.
12/04/1839 The Whig Party meeting in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania nominates William Henry Harrison for President (chosen over Henry Clay and Winfield Scott). John Tyler is unanimously nominated for Vice President.
12/31/1839[Announces peace treaty with Republic of Ecuador](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-4103).
**1840**
01/13/1840[Resubmits treaty to Congress concerning the removal of New York Indians](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-4111). Although there appear to be conflicting interests influencing the tribes, recommends removing the Native Americans as a move that will be beneficial to all.
03/31/1840[Issues Executive Order requiring that all Federal workers work only ten hours per day.](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/executive-order-498)
03/31/1840[Special Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-2082) to Congress relating to a report made by the Secretary of State to resolve the jurisdictional dispute about the schooner Amistad. On August 24, 1839, a U.S. ship captured the Amistad off the coast of Long Island, NY with enslaved Africans onboard. Van Buren sought to extradite the Africans to their Cuban enslavers in an effort to gain pro-slavery votes for his upcoming presidential term.
05/05/1840[Democratic National Convention meeting in Baltimore, MD, nominates Martin Van Buren for a second presidential term](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/1840-democratic-party-platform). However, due to "much diversity of opinion" delegates did not agree on a nominee for Vice President. Instead there was hope that before the election, opinion would coalesce behind a single candidate. The Whig Party and the Abolitionists had conventions in December and November 1839 respectively.
06/27/1840[Recommends creation of exploratory committee to determine northeastern border region](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-3660). This comes after Great Britain and the United States disagree on the northeastern border outlined in Treaty of Paris.
06/29/1840[Sends Special Message to Congress recommending military preparations in case of attack from Great Britain](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-4138).
07/04/1840[Signs Independent Treasury Act](https://uscode.house.gov/statviewer.htm?volume=5&page=385). The Act established an Independent Treasury which was responsible for the collection, transferal, and management of the government’s money supply (5 Stat 385-393).
09/19/1840 The Federal District Court in Hartford, CT rules in the _Amistad_ case that the Africans should be returned to Africa. The US government appeals this decision, and the Supreme Court [decides the case on 03/09/1841](https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/40/518/), holding that the Africans were not slaves but the victims of kidnap.
11/10/1840[Election Day](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/statistics/elections/1840). William Henry Harrison (Whigs) wins 79.6% of the Electoral College and 52.9% of the popular vote, defeating incumbent Van Buren. 80% of the eligible electorate voted in the election, the highest percentage of American turnout at that point.
12/05/1840[Fourth Annual State of the Union Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/fourth-annual-message-4). E xpresses his belief in a peaceful resolution to the British border dispute. Also urges action against the slave trade and forbids citizens from trading with slave factories.
**1841**
02/10/1841 Electoral votes tabulated by Congress.
03/04/1841[Inaugural Address](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/inaugural-address-29) by William Henry Harrison.
**Post-Presidential**
06/22/1848,  
08/09/1848 The [Free Soil Party](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/free-soil-party-platform-1848) meeting in two separate conventions (one at Utica, one at Buffalo), nominate Martin Van Buren for President. He wins no electoral votes.

### [Martin van Buren](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/people/president/martin-van-buren)

8th President of the United States:1837 ‐ 1841

# Martin Van Buren Event Timeline

March 04, 1837

**Martin Van Buren (8) Event Timeline**
**03/04/1837 – 03/04/1841**
05/22/1835 Democratic National Convention in Baltimore Selects Vice President Martin Van Buren as Presidential Nominee.
05/29/1835 Van Buren [formally accepts the nomination](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/message-accepting-the-democratic-presidential-nomination).
11/08/1836[Election Day](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/statistics/elections/1836). Martin Van Buren wins 57.8% of the Electoral College and 50.8% of the popular vote.
12/07/1836 Electors cast their ballots.
**1837**
02/08/1837 Electoral votes tabulated by Congress.
03/04/1837[Inaugural Address](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/inaugural-address-28). Much of Van Buren’s address is spent paying tribute to the Presidents before him.
03/27/1837 US Secretary of State John Forsyth advises that treaties with Mexico preclude US annexation of Texas.
03/28/1837[Proclamation 43C—Extinguishing Title for Indian Lands Between the State of Missouri and the Missouri River](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/proclamation-43-c-extinguishing-title-for-indian-lands-between-the-state-missouri-and-the). The federal government extinguishes all Native American land titles between Missouri and the Missouri River. Native American communities are removed after the United States claimed ownership of the land.
05/10/1837 The Panic of 1837, a financial crisis caused by reckless credit policies for Western land, drives the United States into a recession. The lack of a centralized national bank leaves many local banks to fail.
05/15/1837[Proclamation 43D](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/proclamation-43-d-convening-extra-session-the-congress)--Convening an Extra Session of the Congress in a session to begin 09/04/1837 (see below).
06/27/1837 Receives a set of [Resolves](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/state-maine-resolves-relative-the-northeastern-boundary) from officials in the State of Maine seeking assistance and support in resisting British "usurpations and encroachments," and urging the governor to call on the President to survey and explore the northeastern boundary of the state according to the treaty of 1783.
08/04/1837 The Minister of the Texas Republic [proposes annexation](https://www.tshaonline.org/handbook/entries/annexation) of Texas to the United States.
08/05/1837 Rejects the Republic of Texas’ proposal to annex Texas. Van Buren fears that annexing Texas would compel Mexico to retaliate; cause controversy by adding to slave territory.
09/04/1837 In [Special Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-session-message-7) opening a special session of Congress, calls for Congress to deal with the financial crisis. Suggested actions include a suspension of specie payments.
09/30/1937 By [Special Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-4035), provides the House of Representative with papers relating to the proposed Annexation of Texas. ([View pdf document i](https://www.google.com/books/edition/Documents_Relating_to_the_Foreign_Relati/b64TAAAAYAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=%22to+whom+was+referred+a+resolution+of+the+House+of+Representatives,+dated+the+13th+instant,+requesting%22&pg=RA4-PA94-IA3&printsec=frontcover)ncluding the papers referenced in this Special Message.)
11/12/1837 Newspapers report expectation of immigration to Vermont from Canada due to "serious apprehensions of disturbances in Canada (_Daily Pittsburgh Gazette, 11/13/1837, p. 2)_
11/18/1837 Further newspaper reports of armed conflict in Canada by groups opposed to British rule. (_Daily Pittsburgh Gazette, 11/27/1837, p. 2_
12/05/1837[First Annual Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/first-annual-message-4). Expresses concern about relations with Britain concerning the Maine borderlands. Discusses unsettled US claims against Mexico but makes no mention of the Republic of Texas. Advocates for an independent Treasury system.
12/05/1837 Canadian politician and firebrand [William Lyon Mackenzie](https://www.thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/mackenzie-william-lyon) attempts, near Toronto, to launch a popular rebellion against British colonial rule. Many in the US sympathized with the rebellion and hoped that eventually Canada would become part of the United States. Mackenzie later established a rebel force on Navy Island, not far from Niagara Falls.
12/21/1837[Announces construction of an independent Treasury in order to hold federal funds](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-4044).
12/29/1837 The _Caroline,_ an American steamship that was providing supplies to Canadian rebels on Navy Island (12/05/1837), [is seized by the British-backed Canadian militia](https://www.lawfareblog.com/caroline-affair), set afire, and set adrift to float over the Niagara Falls. At least one American was killed during the raid. News of this event reaches Van Buren on 01/04/1838. In subsequent years, the incident will become important in international law as an instance of "anticipatory self-defense" on the part of the British.
**1838**
01/05/1838 In a [Special Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-4045) to the Congress, expresses concern that existing laws are insufficient to guarantee protection of American borders.
01/05/1838[Proclamation 45A—Neutrality With Respect to Canadian Affairs](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/proclamation-45-neutrality-with-respect-canadian-affairs). Emphasizes a peaceful response to the conflict arising from the _Caroline_ incident.
03/12/1838 In [_Kendall v. United States_](https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/37/524/)the Supreme Court decides 9-0 decides against an expansive view of Presidential power. "To contend that the obligations imposed on the President to see the laws faithfully executed, implies a power to forbid their execution; is a novel construction of the constitution, and is entirely inadmissible."
04/25/1838[Co nvention between the United States and the Republic of Texas](https://avalon.law.yale.edu/19th_century/tex38-2.asp) establishes a commission to survey and mark the international boundary.
05/02/1838 In a [Special Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-3229) to the House, addresses d ispute over attacks on civilian steamboats between Mexico and America.
05/10/1838 In a [Special Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-3298) to the House, suggests that financial difficulties threaten to make the government insolvent.
05/21/1838 In a [Special Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-3408) to the Congress, addresses issues of communication to the Cherokee nation, asking them to move peacefully to the West.
06/12/1838 Signs Act dividing Territory of Wisconsin to establish Territorial Government of Iowa ([5 Stat 235](http://uscode.house.gov/statviewer.htm?volume=5&page=235)).
08/18/1838[The United States Exploring Expedition,](https://www.si.edu/object/united-states-exploring-expedition-1838-1842:auth_exp_fbr_EACE0051) also known as the Wilkes Expedition, departs Norfolk, Virginia. It was commissioned to survey and explore the Pacific Ocean and South Seas. The five ships and crews were provided by the U.S. Navy. The expedition returned in June 1842 having collected vast quantities of flora and fauna that eventually formed the core of the Smithsonian Institution collection (1858).
11/21/1838[Proclamation—Neutrality With Respect to Canadian Affairs](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/proclamation-neutrality-with-respect-canadian-affairs). Van Buren furthers neutrality with Canada, issuing another Proclamation stating that the American government will not assist any Americans engaged in criminal activities with Canada.
12/03/1838 In a Special Message to Congress,delivers his [Second Annual State of the Union Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/second-annual-message-4).
**1839**
02/27/1839[Special Message to Congress regarding conflict with British in the state of Maine](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-3312). Specifically refers to any attempt by Great Britain to enforce its claim on parts of the state of Maine. Authorizes the President to call for up to 50,000 volunteers in the event of conflict.

04/11/1839 A Convention for the Adjustment of Claims between US citizens and the Government of Mexico is signed in Washington. Creates a commission to adjudicate claims. This convention is ratified by the President 04/07/1840 and proclaimed 04/08/1840. ([Link to pdf text of the Convention](https://www.google.com/books/edition/Mexican_Claims/549chErQ0aYC?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=whereas+the+parties+to+said+convention+are+still,+and+equally,+desirous+of+terminating+the+discussion&pg=PA44&printsec=frontcover))
05/13/1839 In a [Special Message to the Senate](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-4092), reports compensation by Great Britain for the brigs, _Enterprise_, _Encomium_, and _Comet_ in which slaves were captured by the British territory of the Bermuda and Bahamas islands.

Van Buren also urges Congress to pass a law to make public officials using public funds for private purposes a crime.
12/04/1839 The Whig Party meeting in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania nominates William Henry Harrison for President (chosen over Henry Clay and Winfield Scott). John Tyler is unanimously nominated for Vice President.
12/31/1839[Announces peace treaty with Republic of Ecuador](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-4103).
**1840**
01/13/1840[Resubmits treaty to Congress concerning the removal of New York Indians](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-4111). Although there appear to be conflicting interests influencing the tribes, recommends removing the Native Americans as a move that will be beneficial to all.
03/31/1840[Issues Executive Order requiring that all Federal workers work only ten hours per day.](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/executive-order-498)
03/31/1840[Special Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-2082) to Congress relating to a report made by the Secretary of State to resolve the jurisdictional dispute about the schooner Amistad. On August 24, 1839, a U.S. ship captured the Amistad off the coast of Long Island, NY with enslaved Africans onboard. Van Buren sought to extradite the Africans to their Cuban enslavers in an effort to gain pro-slavery votes for his upcoming presidential term.
05/05/1840[Democratic National Convention meeting in Baltimore, MD, nominates Martin Van Buren for a second presidential term](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/1840-democratic-party-platform). However, due to "much diversity of opinion" delegates did not agree on a nominee for Vice President. Instead there was hope that before the election, opinion would coalesce behind a single candidate. The Whig Party and the Abolitionists had conventions in December and November 1839 respectively.
06/27/1840[Recommends creation of exploratory committee to determine northeastern border region](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-3660). This comes after Great Britain and the United States disagree on the northeastern border outlined in Treaty of Paris.
06/29/1840[Sends Special Message to Congress recommending military preparations in case of attack from Great Britain](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/special-message-4138).
07/04/1840[Signs Independent Treasury Act](https://uscode.house.gov/statviewer.htm?volume=5&page=385). The Act established an Independent Treasury which was responsible for the collection, transferal, and management of the government’s money supply (5 Stat 385-393).
09/19/1840 The Federal District Court in Hartford, CT rules in the _Amistad_ case that the Africans should be returned to Africa. The US government appeals this decision, and the Supreme Court [decides the case on 03/09/1841](https://supreme.justia.com/cases/federal/us/40/518/), holding that the Africans were not slaves but the victims of kidnap.
11/10/1840[Election Day](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/statistics/elections/1840). William Henry Harrison (Whigs) wins 79.6% of the Electoral College and 52.9% of the popular vote, defeating incumbent Van Buren. 80% of the eligible electorate voted in the election, the highest percentage of American turnout at that point.
12/05/1840[Fourth Annual State of the Union Message](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/fourth-annual-message-4). E xpresses his belief in a peaceful resolution to the British border dispute. Also urges action against the slave trade and forbids citizens from trading with slave factories.

## Statistics, Data and Mapping

#### In analyzing the policy achievements and lasting impact of Presidents, it is often helpful to look at data relating to things such as the electoral context in which the President serves, level and type of presidential activity, and public approval.

#### A common expectation is that the President's success in enacting new legislation is dependent on the size of the President's electoral margin and the degree to which the President's party dominate in Congress. Another common expectation is that the President's success is dependent on favorable levels of public approval.

### We also include information available in other sources, but that are convenient to have in close proximity to the main document collection. An important example is the **[Election Map Data](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/statistics/elections)**.

[![Image 2: 1860 election map](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/sites/default/files/1860_election_map.png)](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/statistics/elections/1860)
_[1860 Election Map](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/statistics/elections/1860)_

#### In the collection, we have maps showing election outcomes by state starting with the [election of 1789](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/statistics/elections/1789). The maps show at a glance the geographical growth of the United States and the shifting political fortunes of different parties. For each presidential election year, we also provide national and state-by-state voting results, both popular and electoral, of the major party candidates. Note that because of 3 rd party candidates, the "total votes" may not precisely equal the sum of the major parties.

### In the [**Data Archive pages**](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/statistics/data)we have assembled a wide array of data of interest spanning the range of indicators that scholars have found useful. In some cases, the data summarize aspects of our own document collection.

#### **[See all](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/statistics/data)**

This is a list of military conflicts, that [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") has been involved in the 19th century from 1801 to 1850.

This list is part of a larger series of list articles that cover the various wars involving the United States from its colonial roots to the present. They are:

The **Second Seminole War**, also known as the **Florida War**, was a conflict from 1835 to 1842 in [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida "Florida") between the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") and groups of people collectively known as [Seminoles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seminole "Seminole"), consisting of [Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscogee "Muscogee") and [Black Seminoles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Seminoles "Black Seminoles") as well as other allied tribes (see below). It was part of a series of conflicts called the [Seminole Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seminole_Wars "Seminole Wars"). The Second Seminole War, often referred to as _the_ Seminole War, is regarded as "the longest and most costly of the [Indian conflicts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Indian_Wars "American Indian Wars") of the United States".[[13]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-13) After the [Treaty of Payne's Landing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Payne's_Landing "Treaty of Payne's Landing") in 1832 that called for the Seminoles' removal from Florida, tensions rose until fierce hostilities occurred in [Dade's massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dade_battle "Dade battle") in 1835. This engagement officially started the war although there were a series of incidents leading up to the Dade battle. The Seminoles and the U.S. forces engaged in mostly small engagements for more than six years. By 1842, only a few hundred native people remained in Florida. Although no peace treaty was ever signed, the war was declared over on August 14, 1842, by Colonel [William Jenkins Worth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Jenkins_Worth "William Jenkins Worth").[[14]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-14)

## Background

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Second_Seminole_War&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Background")]

Bands from various tribes in the [southeastern United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_United_States "Southeastern United States") had moved into the unoccupied lands in Florida in the 18th century. These included [Alabamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alabama_(people) "Alabama (people)"), [Choctaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choctaw "Choctaw"), [Yamasees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yamasee "Yamasee"), [Yuchis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuchi "Yuchi") and [Muscogees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscogee "Muscogee") (then called "Creeks"). The Muscogees were the largest group, and included people from the Lower Towns and Upper Towns of the [Muscogee Confederacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscogee#Rise_of_the_Muscogee_Confederacy "Muscogee"), and both [Hitchiti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikasuki_language "Mikasuki language") and [Muscogee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscogee_language "Muscogee language") speakers. One group of Hitchiti speakers, the Mikasuki, settled around what is now [Lake Miccosukee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Miccosukee "Lake Miccosukee") near [Tallahassee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tallahassee,_Florida "Tallahassee, Florida"). Another group of Hitchiti speakers settled around the [Alachua Prairie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paynes_Prairie "Paynes Prairie") in what is now [Alachua County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alachua_County,_Florida "Alachua County, Florida") (see [Ahaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahaya "Ahaya")). The Spanish in [St. Augustine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Augustine,_Florida "St. Augustine, Florida") began calling the Alachua Muscogees _cimarrones_, which roughly meant "wild ones" or "runaways",[[a]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-16) and which is the probable origin of "Seminole". This name was eventually also applied to the other groups in Florida, although the Native Americans still regarded themselves as members of different tribes. Other groups in Florida at the time of the Seminole Wars included "[Spanish Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Indians "Spanish Indians")", so called because it was believed that they were descended from [Calusas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calusa "Calusa"), and "rancho Indians", persons of Native American ancestry, possibly both Calusa and Muscogee, and mixed Native American/Spanish ancestry, living at Spanish/Cuban [fishing ranchos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fishing_ranchos "Fishing ranchos") on the Florida coast.[[16]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-17) For a brief period after the start of the war, these rancho Indians, particularly those residing along Tampa Bay, were offered protection. However, they were also eventually forced onto reservations.[[17]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBuker199711-18)

[![Image 6](http://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bf/Moultriecreekreservation.PNG/250px-Moultriecreekreservation.PNG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Moultriecreekreservation.PNG)

The Treaty of Moultrie Creek provided for a reservation in central Florida for the Seminoles.

The United States and Spain were at odds over Florida after the [Treaty of Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Paris_(1783) "Treaty of Paris (1783)") ended the [American Revolutionary War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Revolutionary_War "American Revolutionary War") and returned [East](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Florida "East Florida") and [West Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Florida "West Florida") to Spanish control. The United States disputed the boundaries of West Florida. They accused the Spanish authorities of harboring fugitive slaves (see the [Negro Fort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Negro_Fort "Negro Fort")) and of failing to restrain the Native Americans living in Florida from raiding the United States. Starting in 1810, the United States occupied and annexed parts of [West Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_West_Florida "Republic of West Florida"). Also, the [Patriot War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriot_War_(Florida) "Patriot War (Florida)") of 1812 was part of these ongoing conflicts. In 1818, [Andrew Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Jackson "Andrew Jackson") led an invasion of [Spanish Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Florida "Spanish Florida"), during the [War of 1812](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_of_1812 "War of 1812") and the [Creek War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creek_War "Creek War") leading to the [First Seminole War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Seminole_War "First Seminole War").[[18]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-19)

The United States acquired Florida from Spain through the [Adams–Onís Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adams%E2%80%93On%C3%ADs_Treaty "Adams–Onís Treaty") in 1819 and took possession of the territory in 1821. Now that Florida belonged to the United States, settlers pressured the government to remove the Seminole and their allies altogether. In 1823 the government negotiated the [Treaty of Moultrie Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Moultrie_Creek "Treaty of Moultrie Creek") with the Seminoles, establishing a reservation for them in the middle of the territory. Six chiefs, however, were allowed to keep their villages along the [Apalachicola River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apalachicola_River "Apalachicola River") (see [Neamathla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neamathla "Neamathla")).[[19]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-20)

### Move to the reservation

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Second_Seminole_War&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Move to the reservation")]

The Seminoles gave up their lands in the panhandle and slowly settled into the reservation, although they occasionally had clashes with European Americans. Colonel (later General) [Duncan Lamont Clinch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duncan_Lamont_Clinch "Duncan Lamont Clinch") was placed in charge of the Army units in Florida. [Fort King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_King "Fort King") was built near the reservation agency, at the site of present-day [Ocala, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocala,_Florida "Ocala, Florida").[[20]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-21)

By early 1827, the Army reported that the Seminoles were on the reservation and Florida was peaceful. This peace lasted for five years, during which time there were repeated calls for the Seminoles to be sent west of the Mississippi. The Seminoles were opposed to the move, and especially to the suggestion that they should be placed on the Creek reservation. Most European Americans regarded the Seminoles as simply Creeks who had recently moved to Florida, while the Seminoles claimed Florida as their home and denied that they had any connection with the Creeks.[[21]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-22)

The status of runaway slaves was a continuing irritation between Seminoles and European Americans. "The major problem was not with them [Seminoles] but with the Indian-[Negros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Negros "Negros")."[[22]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-Mahon251-23) General Taylor would not, being a _slave holder_ himself, deny "the Seminoles of their Negros", and "in practice", handed his captives over to Lt. J. G. Reynolds, [U.S. Marine Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Marine_Corps "U.S. Marine Corps"), "in charge of immigration."[[22]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-Mahon251-23) Spain had given freedom to slaves who escaped to Florida under their rule, although the U.S. did not recognize it. Over the years, those who became known as [Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Seminoles "Black Seminoles") or Negro [Seminoles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seminoles "Seminoles") established communities separate from the Seminole villages, and the two peoples had close alliances although they maintained separate cultures. "Negroes among the Seminoles constituted a threat to the [institution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institution "Institution") of [slavery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slavery "Slavery") north of the Spanish border.[[23]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-Mahon20-24) Slave holders in Mississippi and other border areas were aware of this and "constantly accused the Indians of stealing their _Negroes._ However, this "accusation" was often reversed; whites were raiding Florida and forcibly stealing the red men's slaves.[[23]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-Mahon20-24)

Worried about the possibility of an Indian uprising and/or an armed slave rebellion, Governor DuVal requested additional Federal troops for Florida. Instead, Fort King was closed in 1828. The Seminoles, short of food and finding the hunting becoming poorer on the reservation, were wandering off of it more often. Also in 1828, Andrew Jackson, the old enemy of the Seminoles, was elected [President of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States"). In 1830 Congress passed the [Indian Removal Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Removal_Act "Indian Removal Act"). They wanted to solve the problems with the Seminoles by moving them to west of the [Mississippi River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi_River "Mississippi River").[[24]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-25)

### Treaty of Payne's Landing

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Second_Seminole_War&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Treaty of Payne's Landing")]

Main article: [Treaty of Payne's Landing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Payne's_Landing "Treaty of Payne's Landing")

In the spring of 1832, the Seminoles on the reservation were called to a meeting at Payne's Landing on the [Oklawaha River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklawaha_River "Oklawaha River"). The treaty negotiated there called for the Seminoles to move west, if the land was found to be suitable. They were to be settled on the Creek reservation and become part of the Creek tribe. The delegation of seven chiefs who were to inspect the new reservation did not leave Florida until October 1832. After the chiefs had toured the area for several months and had conferred with the Creeks who had already been settled there, on March 28, 1833, the federal government produced a treaty with the chiefs' signatures.[[25]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-Missall_83-85-26)

Upon their return to Florida, however, most of the chiefs renounced the statement, claiming that they had not signed it, or that they had been forced to sign it. They said they did not have the power to decide for all the tribes and bands that resided on the reservation. Even some U.S. Army officers claimed that the chiefs had been "wheedled and bullied into signing." Others noted "there is evidence of trickery by the whites in the way the treaty is phrased."[[26]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-27) The members of the villages in the area of the Apalachicola River were more easily persuaded, however, as they suffered more encroachment from European Americans; they went west in 1834.[[25]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-Missall_83-85-26)

[![Image 7](http://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/An_Indian_Town%2C_Residence_of_a_Chief.jpg/250px-An_Indian_Town%2C_Residence_of_a_Chief.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:An_Indian_Town,_Residence_of_a_Chief.jpg)

This view of a Seminole village shows the log cabins they lived in prior to the disruptions of the Second Seminole War.

The [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") finally ratified the [Treaty of Payne's Landing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Payne's_Landing "Treaty of Payne's Landing") in April 1834. The treaty had given the Seminoles three years to move west of the Mississippi. The government interpreted the three years as starting 1832, and expected the Seminoles to move in 1835. Fort King was reopened in 1834. A new Seminole agent, Wiley Thompson, had been appointed in 1834, and the task of persuading the Seminoles to move fell to him. He called the chiefs together at Fort King in October 1834 to talk to them about the removal to the west. The Seminoles informed Thompson that they had no intention of moving, and that they did not feel bound by the Treaty of Payne's Landing. Thompson requested reinforcements for [Fort King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_King "Fort King") and [Fort Brooke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Brooke "Fort Brooke"), reporting that, "the Indians after they had received the Annuity, purchased an unusually large quantity of Powder & Lead." General Clinch also warned Washington that the Seminoles did not intend to move, and that more troops would be needed to force them to move. In March 1835 Thompson called the chiefs together to read a letter from President Andrew Jackson to them. In his letter, Jackson said, "Should you... refuse to move, I have then directed the Commanding officer to remove you by force." The chiefs asked for thirty days to respond. A month later the Seminole chiefs told Thompson that they would not move west. Thompson and the chiefs began arguing, and General Clinch had to intervene to prevent bloodshed. Eventually, eight of the chiefs agreed to move west, but asked to delay the move until the end of the year, and Thompson and Clinch agreed.[[27]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-28)

Five of the most important Seminole chiefs, including [Micanopy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micanopy "Micanopy") of the Alachua Seminoles, had not agreed to the move. In retaliation, Thompson declared that those chiefs were removed from their positions. As relations with the Seminoles deteriorated, Thompson forbade the sale of guns and ammunition to them. [Osceola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osceola "Osceola"), a young warrior beginning to be noticed by the European Americans, was particularly upset by the ban, feeling that it equated Seminoles with slaves and said, "The white man shall not make me black. I will make the white man red with blood; and then blacken him in the sun and rain ... and the buzzard live upon his flesh." In spite of this, Thompson considered Osceola to be a friend, and gave him a rifle. Later, though, when Osceola was causing trouble, Thompson had him locked up at Fort King for a night. The next day, in order to secure his release, Osceola agreed to abide by the Treaty of Payne's Landing and to bring his followers in.[[28]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-29)

The situation grew worse. A group of European Americans assaulted some Indians sitting around a campfire. Two more Indians came up during the assault and opened fire on the European Americans. Three European Americans were wounded, and one Indian was killed and one wounded. In August 1835, Private Kinsley Dalton (for whom [Dalton, Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalton,_Georgia "Dalton, Georgia"), is named) was killed by Seminoles as he was carrying the mail from Fort Brooke to Fort King. In November, Chief Charley Emathla, wanting no part of a war, led his people to Fort Brooke, where they were to board ships to go west. This was considered a betrayal by other Seminoles. Osceola met Charley Emathla on the trail to Fort King and killed him.[[29]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-30)

## The Dade Battle

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Second_Seminole_War&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: The Dade Battle")]

Main article: [Dade Battle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dade_Battle "Dade Battle")

[![Image 8](http://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b1/Florida_massacre_1836.jpeg/250px-Florida_massacre_1836.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Florida_massacre_1836.jpeg)

Fictional massacres depicted in _An Authentic Narrative of the Seminole War._[[30]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-:0-31)

[![Image 9](http://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fe/Seminolesmassacreingwhites.jpg/250px-Seminolesmassacreingwhites.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Seminolesmassacreingwhites.jpg)

Fictional massacres depicted in _An Authentic Narrative of the Seminole War._[[30]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-:0-31)

As the realization that the Seminoles would resist relocation sank in, Florida began preparing for war. The St. Augustine Militia asked the [War Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_War "United States Department of War") for the loan of 500 muskets. Five hundred volunteers were mobilized under Brig. Gen. [Richard K. Call](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_K._Call "Richard K. Call"). Indian war parties raided farms and settlements, and families fled to forts, large towns, or out of the territory altogether. A war party led by Osceola captured a Florida militia supply train, killing eight of its guards and wounding six others. Most of the goods taken were recovered by the militia in another fight a few days later. Sugar plantations along the Atlantic coast south of St. Augustine were destroyed, with many of the slaves on the plantations joining the Seminoles.[[31]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-32)

The U.S. Army had 11 companies, about 550 soldiers, stationed in Florida. [Fort King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_King "Fort King") had only one company of soldiers, and it was feared that they might be overrun by the Seminoles. There were three companies at Fort Brooke, with another two expected on the way, so it was decided to send two companies to Fort King. On December 23, 1835, the two companies, totaling 110 men, left [Fort Brooke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Brooke "Fort Brooke") under the command of Maj. [Francis L. Dade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_L._Dade "Francis L. Dade"). Seminoles shadowed the marching soldiers for five days. On December 28 the Seminoles ambushed the soldiers, and killed all but three of the command, which became known as the [Dade Massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dade_Massacre "Dade Massacre"). Only three white men survived the battle. Pvt Edwin DeCourcey was hunted down and killed by a Seminole the next day. The other two survivors, Pvt Ransom Clarke and Pvt Joseph Sprague, returned to Fort Brooke. Only Clarke, who ultimately succumbed to his wounds 5 years later, dying on November 18, 1840, at the age of 28, left any account of the battle from the Army's perspective. Entitled _"The Surprising Adventures of Ransom Clark, Among the Indians in Florida"_, it was published in 1839 by J. Orlando Orton and "printed by Johnson and Marble in [Binghamton, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Binghamton,_New_York "Binghamton, New York")."[[32]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-33)[[b]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-34) Joseph Sprague suffered a "[shattered](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone_fracture "Bone fracture")[arm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arm "Arm")",[[33]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-Laumer266-35) served in the army until March 1843, and lived out his days near [White Springs, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Springs,_Florida "White Springs, Florida"), until possibly 1848. No written material from Sprague's personal military [experience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Experience "Experience")'s has ever surfaced.[[33]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-Laumer266-35) The Seminoles lost three men killed, with five wounded. On the same day as the Dade Massacre, Osceola and his followers shot and killed [Wiley Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wiley_Thompson "Wiley Thompson") and six others outside of Fort King.[[34]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-36)

In February, Major [Ethan Allen Hitchcock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethan_A._Hitchcock_(general) "Ethan A. Hitchcock (general)") was among those who found the remains of the Dade party. In his journal he wrote about the discovery and vented his bitter discontent with the conflict:

> The government is in the wrong, and this is the chief cause of the persevering opposition of the Indians, who have nobly defended their country against our attempt to enforce a fraudulent treaty. The natives used every means to avoid a war, but were forced into it by the tyranny of our government.[[35]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-37)

On December 29, General Clinch left Fort Drane (recently established on Clinch's plantation, about twenty miles (32 km) northwest of Fort King) with 750 soldiers, including 500 volunteers on an enlistment due to end January 1, 1836. They were going to a Seminole stronghold called the [Cove of the Withlacoochee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cove_of_the_Withlacoochee "Cove of the Withlacoochee"), an area of many lakes on the southwest side of the [Withlacoochee River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Withlacoochee_River_(Florida) "Withlacoochee River (Florida)"). When they reached the river, they could not find the ford, and Clinch had his regular troops ferried across the river in a single canoe they had found. Once they were across and had relaxed, the Seminoles attacked. The troops survived only by fixing bayonets and charging the Seminoles, at the cost of four dead and 59 wounded. The militia provided cover as the Army troops withdrew across the river.[[36]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-38)

On January 6, 1836, a band of Seminoles attacked the [coontie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coontie "Coontie") plantation of [William Cooley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Cooley "William Cooley") on the [New River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_River_(Broward_County,_Florida) "New River (Broward County, Florida)") (in present-day [Fort Lauderdale, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Lauderdale,_Florida "Fort Lauderdale, Florida")), killing his wife and children and the children's tutor. The other residents of the New River area and of the [Biscayne Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biscayne_Bay "Biscayne Bay") country to the south fled to Key West.[[37]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-39) On January 17, volunteers and Seminoles met south of St. Augustine at the [Battle of Dunlawton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunlawton_Plantation_and_Sugar_Mill "Dunlawton Plantation and Sugar Mill"). The volunteers lost four men, with thirteen wounded.[[38]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-40) On January 19, 1836, the Navy [sloop-of-war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sloop-of-war "Sloop-of-war")[_Vandalia_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Vandalia_(1828) "USS Vandalia (1828)") was dispatched to Tampa Bay from Pensacola. On the same day 57 [U.S. Marines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps "United States Marine Corps") were dispatched from Key West to help man Fort Brooke.[[39]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-41)

## General Gaines' expedition

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Second_Seminole_War&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: General Gaines' expedition")]

The regular American army was very small at the time, with fewer than 7,500 men manning a total of 53 posts.[[40]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-42) It was spread thin, with the Canada–U.S. border to guard, coastal fortifications to man, and especially, Indians to move west and then watch and keep separated from white settlers. Temporary needs for additional troops were filled by state and territory militias, and by self-organized volunteer units. As news and rumors of the fighting spread, action was taken on many levels. Maj. Gen. [Winfield Scott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winfield_Scott "Winfield Scott") was placed in charge of the war. Congress appropriated US$620,000 for the war. Volunteer companies began forming in Alabama, Georgia and [South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina "South Carolina"). General [Edmund P. Gaines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmund_P._Gaines "Edmund P. Gaines") put together a force of 1,100 regulars and volunteers in [New Orleans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans") and sailed with them to Fort Brooke.[[41]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-43) A lack of arms was also an issue, with only two arsenals located in Florida, one at Fort Brooke and the other at Fort Marion, with a third under construction in what is now [Chattahoochee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chattahoochee,_Florida "Chattahoochee, Florida").[[42]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-44)

[![Image 10](http://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2e/Dademassacresite.jpg/250px-Dademassacresite.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dademassacresite.jpg)

_Viewing the demise of Major Dade and his Command_

When Gaines reached Fort Brooke, he found it low on supplies. Believing that General Scott had sent supplies to Fort King, Gaines led his men on to Fort King. Along the road they found the site of the Dade Massacre, and buried the bodies in three mass graves. The force reached Fort King after nine days, only to find it was very short on supplies. After receiving seven days' worth of rations from General Clinch at Fort Drane, Gaines headed back for Fort Brooke. Hoping to accomplish something for his efforts, Gaines took his men on a different route back to Fort Brooke, intending to engage the Seminoles in their stronghold in the Cove of the Withlacoochee River. Due to a lack of knowledge of the country, the Gaines party reached the same point on the Withlacoochee where Clinch had met the Seminoles one-and-a-half months earlier, and it took another day to find the ford while the two sides exchanged gunfire across the river.[[43]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-45)

When a crossing was attempted at the ford of the Withlacoochee, Lt. James Izard was wounded (and later died), and General Gaines was stuck by a bullet. Unable to ford the river, and not having enough ration to return to Fort King, Gaines and his men constructed a fortification, called Camp Izard, and sent word to General Clinch. Gaines hoped that the Seminoles would concentrate around Camp Izard, and that Clinch's forces could then hit the Seminoles in their flank, crushing them between the two forces. General Scott, however, who was in charge of the war, ordered Clinch to stay at Fort Drane. Gaines's men were soon reduced to eating their horses and mules, and an occasional dog, while a battle went on for eight days. Still at Fort Drane, Clinch requested that General Scott change his orders and allow him to go to Gaines' aid. Clinch finally decided to disobey Scott and left to join Gaines just one day before Scott's permission to do so arrived at Fort Drane. Clinch and his men reached Camp Izard on March 6, chasing away the Seminoles.[[44]](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Seminole_War#cite_note-46)

## General Scott's campaign

[[edit](http://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Second_Seminole_War&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: General Scott's campaign")]

[![Image 11](http://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/Pilaklikaha.png/250px-Pilaklikaha.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Pilaklikaha.png)

Gen. Eustis burned Pilaklikaha, or Abraham's Town, on his way to join Gen. Scott's campaign.

General Scott had begun assembling men and supplies for a grand campaign against the Seminoles. Three columns, totaling 5,000 men, were to converge on the Cove of the Withlacoochee, trapping the Seminoles with a force large enough to defeat them. Scott would accompany one column, under the command of General Clinch, moving south from [Fort Drane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Drane "Fort Drane"). A second column, under Brig. Gen. [Abraham Eustis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Eustis "Abraham Eustis"), would travel southwest from Volusia, a town on the [St. Johns River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Johns_River "St. Johns River"). The third wing, under the command of Col. William Lindsay, would move north from [Fort Brooke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Brooke "Fort Brooke"). The plan was for the three columns to arrive at the Cove simultaneously so as to prevent the Seminoles from escaping.
